source.title: Accelerated Large Batch Optimization of BERT Pretraining in 54 minutes
source.authors: Shuai Zheng; Haibin Lin; Sheng Zha; Mu Li

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a larger mini-batch can retain held-out task performance using a different optimizer and learning-rate schedule; it does not directly measure the train–test error gap.
record.gate_note: Table 2 includes a 64K/32K LAMB result attributed to prior work [30]; it is not extracted as a study result. The study's own 96K/33K LAMB run diverges, while LANS at the same batch sizes reaches the reported dev-set F1.
record.test_reason: The study reports its optimizer's performance at one batch-size pair. Its own comparison changes the optimizer at the same batch sizes; the smaller-batch result comes from prior work. It therefore does not establish a batch-size penalty or its removal under a fixed epoch budget.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: LANS and the proposed learning-rate schedule enable BERT pretraining with batch sizes 96K/33K in about 54 minutes, reaching the target SQuAD development F1.
record.recipe_differences: Uses LANS, per-block gradient normalization, and a constant learning-rate phase; compares large-batch pretraining rather than measuring a train–test gap.
record.method_sensitivity: At batch sizes 96K/33K, LAMB diverged while LANS with the proposed schedule reached the target dev score.

fits_no_version.finding: At batch sizes 96K/33K and 4301 pretraining steps, LAMB diverges while LANS reaches 90.60 SQuAD development F1 in 53.6 minutes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An adapted optimizer and learning-rate schedule can enable successful BERT pretraining at batch sizes where the tested LAMB configuration diverges.

record.problems: No fixed-epoch comparison with a small-batch run is reported; the 64K/32K LAMB result is attributed to prior work. The reported evaluation is downstream SQuAD dev F1 rather than train and test error.
record.rows_left_out: The 64K/32K LAMB result in Table 2 is attributed to [30] and was left out as a cited prior-work result.

untested.parts: Held-out error across widths beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
The large-versus-small-batch held-out performance difference under fixed epochs, and whether recipe changes remove that difference in a matched comparison.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Accuracy after removing memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: BERT is a language model, contrary to the record's untested-parts statement. Downstream development F1 is a valid held-out performance measure; the decisive limitation is the missing matched batch-size comparison. The cited 64K/32K result is already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.
Width beyond interpolation and test error across widths are not tested.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures are not compared.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD on held-out performance are not tested.

The paper does not hold epochs fixed while comparing large and small batches; the smaller-batch LAMB result is cited from prior work. It reports downstream SQuAD dev F1, not train–test error gaps, and does not test language models.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gaps are not measured.
Removing memorized examples is not tested.

rows.subject: BERT-Large
rows.measure: F1 score on SQuAD-v1.1 development set
rows.note: The larger-batch LAMB run diverged; no dev F1 is reported.
rows.check: Divergence is correctly transcribed, but it does not measure a held-out performance penalty from increasing batch size under a fixed epoch budget. No F1 value is available; 'absent' is unjustified.

rows.subject: BERT-Large
rows.operation_detail: LANS with the proposed learning-rate schedule
rows.measure: F1 score on SQuAD-v1.1 development set
rows.note: This is the study's large-batch result; the paper says it achieves the target accuracy.
rows.check: 90.60 dev F1 is correctly transcribed. Reaching the target with LANS demonstrates method performance, but without a matched smaller-batch comparison it cannot establish whether a batch-size penalty was removed. Fine-tuning also uses AdamW with blockwise gradient normalization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The larger-batch LAMB run diverged (R1), while LANS with a modified recipe reached 90.60 dev F1 at those batch sizes (R2); the study does not provide a fixed-epoch small-batch comparison.
